summary: The round 8 fixes close what they set out to do. Every check on the shaper's output now runs from one function, ids are numbered from one helper, a collapse must name what it collapses into, and an own-file call is left to the person. All seven candidates were verified. The correctness finding is that R5-3's rename of coverage refs reads an id differently from accountCoverage, so an id followed by '.' or '/', or a duplicate's ref with a note, still mints a duplicate finding. The six nits sit at the edges of R8-2, R8-4 and R8-5: an `own` flag beside a made-up rule, two resolve bullets that conflict, a reshape prompt without secondLook, an own-file check keyed on the label alone, a heading order the docs pin, and a regex written twice. The repository has no scheduled or queued work.

findings.title: A finding on Redline's own files is stored as a made-up rule plus an `own` flag, and every reader has to branch on the flag
findings.description: R8-4 records a finding on Redline's own files as `{ rule: OWN_FILE, own: true, reason: OWN_FILE_REASON }` (line 2921). OWN_FILE is a why_human label (line 353), not an ask rule. The flag is then copied from shape to shape, and each reader branches on it. The copies are in leftDecision (1209, 1213), outcomesFor (2688), result().forced (2362), the decisions loop in resolveWith (3192-3193), deferredAll (3409), the resolve prompt (1830), the handoff's Left-to heading (3578) and leftToYou (3619). leftUnder (356) is called from replyBody, describeOutcome, threadCandidates and the autopilot log. That is about fourteen sites. Because `rule` is still set, any reader that checks `rule` and forgets `own` treats the finding as covered by a repository rule. R9-4 is one case of this: both resolve-prompt bullets apply. No behaviour is wrong beyond R9-4. All of this code is R8-4's, in the fix diff.
findings.proposedFix: Give a finding on Redline's own files one synthetic entry with the same shape as an ask rule, for example `OWN_RULE = { id: OWN_FILE, reason: OWN_FILE_REASON, label: "Redline's own files", under: "the rule on Redline's own files" }`. Have forceAskRules record `rule` and the display wording from that entry, so readers use the entry's fields and no reader branches on `own`.

findings.title: The regex that reads a duplicate's target index is now written twice
findings.description: R8-2 added `targetOf` in accountCoverage (line 1652). It reads a duplicate ref's target with `/^(?:(?:candidate|index)\s+)?(\d+)\b/i`. review()'s set-aside builder reads the same target with the same regex, written again at line 2539. The two copies are identical today, so nothing disagrees yet. A later change to one form (say `candidate #3`) that misses the other would make namesNothing and the block's `into` read different targets for the same ref.
findings.proposedFix: Hoist one helper, for example `const duplicateTarget = (ref) => Number((/^(?:(?:candidate|index)\s+)?(\d+)\b/i.exec(ref || '') || [])[1]) || 0`, and call it from targetOf and from the set-aside builder.

findings.title: Every reshape now runs checkSecondLook, but the reshape prompt's list of return fields leaves out secondLook
findings.description: Since R8-5, vetShape (lines 3106-3122) runs checkSecondLook on every reshape (line 3115). The shaper's output schema makes the field optional (line 740). The shape prompt asks for secondLook on a finding the verifier could not confirm (line 1755). The reshape prompt's list (line 1812) names only id, disposition, decidedBy, recommendation and the reason for a decline. The agent file's rule 10 does ask for secondLook (agents/redline-shaper.md:32). A reshape that returns only the fields the prompt lists triggers 'the shaper gave no second look' (line 2791) for every unconfirmed finding, including ones the first shape answered. checkSecondLook's other test, a 'could not confirm' decline whose second look says otherwise (line 2794), only runs when secondLook is present, so it is skipped on that reshape. Needs a plan bounce on a round with an unconfirmed finding. Before R8-5 the reshape never ran checkSecondLook.
findings.proposedFix: Add the field to the reshape prompt's return list, as the shape prompt words it: '..., and reason for a decline; for a finding the verifier could not confirm also secondLook'. Add a loop check: a bounce on a round with an unconfirmed finding, where the reshape returns secondLook, raises no second-look warning.

findings.title: When the repository declares ask rules, a decided call on Redline's own files gets both resolve-prompt bullets, and their wording conflicts
findings.description: resolveWith sets `decision.rule = forced.rule` on every forced decision (line 3191), so a call on Redline's own files carries `rule: "redline's own file"` (line 2921) as well as `own: true` (3192-3193). leftDecision does the same on autopilot (lines 1212-1213). resolvePrompt adds the `rule` bullet whenever `askRules.length` (line 1828). It adds the `own` bullet whenever a decision has `own` (line 1830). In a repository with ask rules, the resolve agent therefore gets both bullets for one decision. The rule bullet says to write the plan task as 'Left to the person: <id> (repository rule redline's own file)' and the Deferred mitigation as 'none (repository rule redline's own file)'. The own bullet says '(Redline's own files)' and 'none (the rule on Redline's own files)'. The workflow posts the second form: the deferred mitigation is `none (${leftUnder(forced)})` (line 3409). So shape.md and plan.md can carry the first form, or a mix, and disagree with what is posted. Needs a repository that declares askRules and a round with a decided call on Redline's own files. R9-1 shows the same cause in the wider code.
findings.proposedFix: Scope the rule bullet's wording to decisions without `own` ('A decision carrying `rule` and no `own` ...'). Or stop copying `rule` onto own decisions in resolveWith and leftDecision. Add a loop check: with askRules declared and a decided own-file call, the resolve prompt names only the own-file wording for that id.

findings.title: A coverage ref whose renamed id is followed by '.' or '/' is not renamed, so accountCoverage mints a duplicate correctness finding
findings.description: R5-3 was fixed, but still reproduces for some ref forms. review() renames a verified or unconfirmed ref's leading token, read with `/^[^\s:,;()]+/` (line 2512). That token runs on through '.', '/' and other punctuation. accountCoverage reads the leading id with `/^(R\d+-\d+)(?![\w-])/` (line 1621), which stops before them. Traced for round 3: the reviewer returns finding id 'R2-1', which is renamed R3-4 (lines 2445-2452, where renamed holds 'R2-1'), and coverage `{outcome: 'verified', ref: 'R2-1. still reproduces'}`. The token is 'R2-1.', which renamed does not hold, so the ref keeps 'R2-1'. accountCoverage then reads the id 'R2-1', which byId no longer has. It warns 'not a finding of this round' (1627-1628), and the mint loop adds R3-5 as an unconfirmed correctness finding beside R3-4 for the same candidate. 'R2-1/x' behaves the same way. A dash after the id ('R2-1-x') is minted whatever the rename does, since line 1621's lookahead rejects it. The fix diff adds a duplicate-ref variant. review() renames a duplicate's ref only when it is the whole ref (lines 2504-2510, token '' for duplicates). So 'R2-1: same cause' keeps the old id, and R8-2's namesNothing (lines 1658-1660) then mints the candidate when no finding of this round, this run or the PR's earlier runs has R2-1. When an earlier round does have an R2-1, the duplicate is counted against that unrelated finding instead. Conditions: two reviewer slips at once, an id outside the round's form plus a ref with punctuation after it. The minted finding is correctness, so it is posted, shaped and can buy a round. The node tool is refused for the reviewer, so this was traced, not run.
findings.proposedFix: Read a ref's leading id in one place, with the same reading accountCoverage uses (an id shape followed by anything but a word character or dash, or a token up to whitespace or punctuation including '.' and '/'). Map it through `renamed` for verified, unconfirmed, duplicate and settled refs alike, keeping the note; a ref that opens with an index can never match a renamed id. Add a loop check modeled on tests/loop-test.mjs:1711, with ref 'R0-1. the lock' and a duplicate ref 'R0-1: same cause', expecting one finding R1-1 and nothing minted.

findings.title: Whether a finding is on Redline's own files is decided by the shaper's why_human label alone, never by the finding's path
findings.description: forceAskRules records an own-file entry only when the shaper returned `ask` with a call whose why_human is exactly OWN_FILE (lines 2919-2921). Paths rules are matched on the finding's file and on the task's files (ruleForPaths, line 2911). docs/running.md says a finding on `.claude/redline/`, `.claude/redline*.json` or `.claude/settings*.json` 'is put to you the same way ... and on autopilot it is listed under Deferred with no mitigation'. The code keeps that promise only when the shaper uses the label. A finding on `.claude/settings.json` that the shaper sorts as `fix`, or asks about under another case, gets no forced entry. Autopilot then decides it through autopilotDecision (line 3157), and the guard refuses the implementer's write. The reverse also holds: the label on an ordinary file leaves that finding to the person on every dial. Two readings: (a) the shaper's rule 7 is the contract, and the label is enough; (b) the docs' path list is the contract, and forceAskRules should match the finding's file and task files against the own-path globs, as it does for paths rules. Needs the shaper to label a finding differently from rule 7 (agents/redline-shaper.md:28).
findings.proposedFix: Under reading (b), match `[f.file].concat(files)` against the own-path globs the shaper's rule 7 lists, alongside the why_human check, and record the own entry when either holds. Add a loop check: a `.claude/settings.json` finding the shaper sorts as fix is left to the person on autopilot.

findings.title: The Left-to heading orders its two groups by whichever forced entry comes first, but docs/running.md promises one order
findings.description: handoffComment builds the heading's words with `unique(rounds.flatMap(... x.own ? "Redline's own files" : 'repository rules'))` (line 3578). `unique` keeps first-seen order (line 419). record.forced is filled in inScope order by forceAskRules, so the first forced finding of the earliest round sets the order. When a round's first forced finding is on Redline's own files and a later one is under a repository rule, the heading reads `### Left to @x (Redline's own files and repository rules)`. docs/running.md:154 promises `(repository rules and Redline's own files)`.
findings.proposedFix: Build the words in a fixed order: `[hasRule && 'repository rules', hasOwn && "Redline's own files"].filter(Boolean).join(' and ')`. Add a loop check where the own-file finding comes first.

list.summary: When the workflow renames a reviewer's id, a coverage ref that names the old id is no longer updated if the id is followed by '.', '/' or a dash. The rename reads that ref's leading id differently from accountCoverage (line 1621), so the R5-3 fix still mints a duplicate finding for refs like these.
list.failure_scenario: In round 3 the reviewer returns a finding with id "R2-1", which is renamed R3-4. A coverage entry {outcome: 'verified', ref: 'R2-1. still reproduces'} is not updated, because the rename looks up the token "R2-1.". accountCoverage then reads the id "R2-1", which byId no longer has, warns that it is not a finding of this round, and mints R3-5 as an unconfirmed correctness finding that duplicates R3-4. The duplicate is posted inline and shaped. A duplicate ref such as 'R2-1: same cause' goes through the same missed rename and, since R8-2, is minted when no list names R2-1.

list.summary: A decision on an own-file finding carries both `rule` (set to "redline's own file") and `own`. When the repository declares ask rules, the resolve prompt therefore gives the resolve agent two conflicting instructions for the same decision (lines 1828 and 1831).
list.failure_scenario: A repository has askRules, and a round has an own-file call decided on autopilot or by the person. The rule bullet says to write the task as "Left to the person: <id> (repository rule redline's own file)" with Deferred mitigation "none (repository rule redline's own file)". The own bullet says "(Redline's own files)" and "none (the rule on Redline's own files)". shape.md and plan.md can end up with the wrong wording, or a mix of both, and the result disagrees with what the workflow posts.

list.summary: Since R8-5, vetShape runs checkSecondLook on every reshape, but the reshape prompt's list of fields to return leaves out `secondLook`.
list.failure_scenario: A plan bounce on a round with unconfirmed findings. A shaper that follows the reshape prompt omits `secondLook`, so each bounce adds a 'the shaper gave no second look' warning for every unconfirmed finding, even ones the first shape answered. With the field missing, the check that a 'could not confirm' decline agrees with its second look is also skipped on the reshape.

list.summary: The order of the handoff's Left-to heading depends on which forced entry comes first, but docs/running.md:154 documents one fixed order.
list.failure_scenario: A round's first forced finding is on Redline's own files and a later one is under a repository rule. The heading reads '### Left to @x (Redline's own files and repository rules)', while the doc promises '(repository rules and Redline's own files)'.

list.summary: Altitude: whether a finding counts as being on Redline's own files is decided only by the shaper's `why_human` label, never by the finding's path. Paths rules, by contrast, are matched on the path (ruleForPaths).
list.failure_scenario: The shaper asks about a `.claude/settings.json` finding under another case, such as 'outside the pull request'. No forced entry is written, so autopilot decides it and the guard then blocks the implementer. The reverse also happens: a label used by mistake on an ordinary file leaves it to the person on every dial. Matching the finding's file and its task's files against Redline's own-path globs, as forceAskRules already does for paths rules, would make this deterministic.

list.summary: Simplification: an own-file finding is stored as a fake rule (`rule: OWN_FILE`) plus an `own` flag. That takes about 17 `own ?` branches across the workflow and causes the dual `rule`/`own` resolve conflict above.
list.failure_scenario: leftDecision, resolveWith, outcomesFor, leftUnder, leftToYou, the Deferred and Left-to lines, threadCandidates and result().forced each branch on `own`. Each new reader has to remember the flag, and the resolve prompt already got it wrong. One synthetic ask-rule object with id, reason and display wording would give every reader a single shape.

list.summary: Reuse: the regex that finds a duplicate's target (`/^(?:(?:candidate|index)\s+)?(\d+)\b/i`) is now written twice, in accountCoverage's targetOf (line 1652) and in review()'s set-aside builder.
list.failure_scenario: If one copy changes (for example to accept 'candidate #3') and the other does not, namesNothing and the set-aside block's `into` will disagree about which candidate a duplicate points at. review() should call one shared helper.
